title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 3-5). Grothendieck is setting up an 'isotopic category' of oriented surfaces of finite type, with finite étale immersions up to isotopy as morphisms. The goal is to understand the Galois / outer action on fundamental groups and Teichmüller towers.

On the previous page he proved that two finite étale immersions f, g : X → Y are isotopic iff g = f∘u with u a self-homeomorphism of X isotopic to the identity. This uses the factorization f = p∘f_0 through a finite étale cover p : Y' → Y. The next page asks whether that factorization is unique up to unique isomorphism. That reduces to question (11): if γ is a Y-automorphism of Y' (necessarily of finite order) with γ∘f_0 isotopic to f_0, is γ the identity? Taking f_0 = id, the question becomes: is a finite-order automorphism of an oriented finite-type surface Y' that is isotopic to the identity necessarily the identity?

This page does four things.
(i) It treats the ramified case: for a cyclic group generated by γ, one removes the finite set S' of ramification (fixed) points of the action and replaces Y' by Y' \ S'. This reduces to the free (étale) case.
(ii) It warns that the uniqueness property fails without restriction. For Y' = C* or Y' = U×U (U the circle, so a torus), translations by torsion points have finite order and are isotopic to the identity, yet are not the identity.
(iii) Proposition 2. Let Y' be an oriented surface of finite type (compact minus finitely many points) that is 'anabelian': every component Y'_i has χ(Y'_i) < 0, i.e. 2g_i + ν_i ≥ 3 with ν_i the number of punctures. Then every finite-order automorphism γ of Y'_i isotopic to the identity is the identity.
(iv) Strengthening. Since γ preserves components, one may assume Y' connected. In fact it suffices that γ acts trivially on H_1 (or H^1) with coefficients in Z, or even in Z/nZ with n ≥ 3.

The proof is not on this page. The next page hints at the standard argument: a nontrivial orientation-preserving periodic map has isolated fixed points, each of local index +1. Extend γ to the compactification and compare the Lefschetz number, computed from the trivial action on homology, with χ < 0; this gives a contradiction. For the mod-n version, use Serre's rigidity argument.

In modern terms this is the classical fact that Mod(S_{g,ν}) acts faithfully on the isotopy classes of periodic maps (Nielsen / Hurwitz). It is also Serre's lemma that the level-n congruence subgroup, n ≥ 3, of the mapping class group is torsion-free. Here it is used to show that, for hyperbolic surfaces, the isotopic category behaves rigidly: automorphism groups are 'discrete' and factorizations are unique.
errors: The literal claim 'trivial action on H_1(Y'; Z/n), n ≥ 3, implies γ = id' needs care for punctured surfaces, where H_1 includes the puncture loops. For g = 0 one must check that trivial action forces each puncture to be fixed; it does for ν ≥ 3 and n ≥ 3, and then a Möbius map fixing ≥ 3 points is the identity. So the statement is correct, but the page gives no argument.
In (ii), C* is not of 'anabelian' type (χ = 0), and neither is the torus. These examples are correctly offered as exceptions, not errors.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is classical: Nielsen/Hurwitz rigidity plus Serre's level-n lemma, applied to build a rigid isotopic category of surfaces. The only mildly notable point is historical. If the archive date ('from 1978') is accurate, this is possibly early use of the word 'anabélienne' before the 1983 Faltings letter. That date is uncertain.
transcription_corrections: The 'unisog...' word with crossed-out material probably reads 'unicité' or similar: 'la propriété d'unicité (sur les automorph. d'ordre fini de la surface Y') n'est pas vérifiée sans restriction'.
'U×U' is likely the circle group squared, i.e. a torus; consistent with translations by points of finite order.
The line before 'Y' connexe' should read roughly: 'Comme γ conserve (respecte) les composantes connexes, on peut supposer Y' connexe.'
'ou même dans Z/nZ avec n ≥ 3': 'même' is an insertion above the line. H^1 and H_1 are both written as alternatives above 'homologie'.

The opening line '(en gardant les droits types vrai...' is unreliable. It likely concerns reducing to the case of a cyclic subgroup generated by γ ('le cas d'un même sous-groupe de γ'), then removing ramification points S'.
